LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 15.3.1 SENTENCES- 15.3.1.1 IMPERATIVE – COMMANDS, REQUESTS 15.3.1.2 EXCLAMATORY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.3: Grammar in use 15.3.1 Sentences- 15.3.1.1 Imperative – commands, requests 15.3.1.2 Exclamatory
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in use 15.3.1 Sentences- 15.3.1.1 Imperative – commands, requests 15.3.1.2 Exclamatory, part of Strand 15 in Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: When do you use an exclamatory or an imperative sentence in school?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify instances where the two types of sentences are used correctly in printed handouts or online texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in use 15.3.1 Sentences- 15.3.1.1 Imperative – commands, requests 15.3.1.2 Exclamatory in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. punctuate given texts by use of the appropriate punctuation marks,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in use 15.3.1 Sentences- 15.3.1.1 Imperative – commands, requests 15.3.1.2 Exclamatory in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the use of exclamatory and imperative sentences in spoken language.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. orally list the kinds of rules that they would want implemented in their school,
2. identify and label sentence types in a given text,
3. construct imperative sentences as they respond to teacher’s questions,
4. in pairs, construct exclamatory sentences based on one of the characters in a text . 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in use 15.3.1 Sentences- 15.3.1.1 Imperative – commands, requests 15.3.1.2 Exclamatory together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: It is promoted as the learner identifies target sentences from recorded texts.

• Learning to learn: It is enhanced as the learner appreciates the comparison captured in different texts.

Values:
Social justice: It is enhanced as the learner compares societal issues through discussing rules in school.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Problem solving: It is enhanced as the learner works in pairs/groups to construct exclamatory sentences.

Links to other Learning Areas:
